brief: A borrower returns the only item of a loan on the same day it was lent. The desk takes the item back, hands the deposit back in cash, and prints a slip for the return. Choose an item that needs no induction and an assistant who may lend and take returns within the item's deposit. Check the stored loan line is marked returned, the loan's total is back to zero, and the slip shows the deposit handed back.

review.by: the orchestrator (Claude), on the owner's instruction of 2026-10-08 to author, review and commit the scenario; the owner's own review of the committed scenario stays open
review.verdict: kept as the planner wrote it; the files below are the planner's, byte for byte
notes: The brief's 'an item that needs no induction' cannot be expressed through the LendableItem query, which has no inductionRequired argument (ItemsTriggering has one); the planner chose perDay: false, and the resolver's order (deposit, then code) picks an item that needs no induction on both seeds (the cheapest counted item: HND-003 on seed A, T1002 on seed B), so the brief holds without being stated; recorded as a DSL gap in docs/TODO.md.

The brief's 'the loan's total is back to zero': the desk posts a return as a posting of its own (a second loan.posted event with returning: true), whose total is the deposit negated, and leaves the lent posting's total as it was; the scenario checks both postings (the lent one's total equal to the deposit, the return's equal to its negation, Money.negate), which is the desk's reading of 'back to zero': the two postings net to zero.

The slip check (slip.last.loanId of the return posting, its text containing RETURN and the refund amount) is the brief's 'the slip shows the deposit handed back'; the deposit verb with no amount settles the amount due, which on a return is the refund in cash.
The planner's own run (--run, live on seed A) passed; the bindings of both seeds were approved with skillroy resolve (label approve, tier (a) only) after this review.
